correctness.rationale: For n=rm+1 the orthogonal Laplacian eigenspaces have eigenvalues 0 (constants), 1 (r−1 blade-balanced modes), m+1 (r(m−1) blade-internal modes), and n (one hub-against-blades mode). The stated projectors therefore give the exact G=L^+ and G². Writing s=e_a+e_b and d=e_a−e_b, the two diagonal leader penalties equal κ(ssᵀ+ddᵀ)/2. Eliminating the constant mode by the Schur complement leaves L restricted to 1-perp plus κddᵀ/2; applying Sherman–Morrison gives exactly J=n/(2κ)+tr G+(n/4)sᵀGs−κ[dᵀG²d+(n/4)(sᵀGd)²]/(2+κdᵀGd). All possible two-vertex sets belong to exactly A (hub/peripheral), B (same blade), C (distinct blades). Projector substitution yields all three rational formulas in RESULT.md, independently cross-checked by direct rational inverse for six r,m,κ triples. Symbolic simplification independently reproduced JB−JA=m(r−1)(3κ+2m+2)/[2(m+1)(κ+m+1)]>0 and JC−JA=P/[2(m+1)(κ+m+1)(2κ+m+1)], P=(r−2)m(2κ+m+1)²−4κ²−(m²+8m+7)κ−(m+1)². For r=2, P<0. For r≥3, P strictly grows with r and at r=3 equals 4(m−1)κ²+(m+1)(3m−7)κ+(m−1)(m+1)²; for m≥3 all coefficients positive and at m=2 it is 4κ²−3κ+9>0 (discriminant −135). Hence C uniquely minimizes when r=2 and A uniquely minimizes when r≥3, modulo graph automorphisms, for EVERY integer r,m≥2 and finite real κ>0, without gain-dependent ties.
residual_risks: Finite independent inverse tests are not a proof for infinite r,m and continuous κ; analytical Schur complement and polynomial signs are decisive.
Normalization uses unit conductance and equal leader gains; κ=0 excluded and no mixed-noise/generalized gains claim is proved.

value.rationale: The two-leader placement problem with finite pinning gains is a motivated stochastic-control graph-design problem; choosing where to place leaders affects total steady-state variance. The theorem completely solves the optimal pair and exact objective over the natural two-parameter clique-windmill family. It establishes a non-obvious structural phase discontinuity at three blades: with two blades the central maximum-degree hub is strictly suboptimal, while with three or more it is indispensable in every optimal pair; this holds for all finite positive gain strengths and clique sizes, with no ties up to automorphism. These strict gain-uniform inequalities give reusable exact benchmarks for placement heuristics and show why degree-only placement can fail, without inventing a downstream theorem. This is more than a routine isolated numerical example or a mere coefficient calculation; the result concerns an infinite graph family and a sharp parameter boundary. It does not address heterogeneous gains, nonuniform noise/edge conductance, singular zero gain or three-plus leaders.
residual_risks: Historical priority could be weakened by existing windmill-specific finite-gain solutions, especially Sun–Li–Liu 2020; value pertains to exact all-parameter structural classification if not already known.
The formula does not generalize established optimality to unequal gains or other noise models.

final_claim: For W_{r,m}=K_1∨(rK_m), integers r,m≥2 with unit conductances, exactly two distinct equally weighted finite-gain leaders and κ>0, minimize J(S)=tr[L+κdiag(1_S)]^{-1}. The unique optimal automorphism orbit is two peripheral vertices in distinct blades if r=2, and the hub plus one peripheral vertex if r≥3, with strict inequalities for all finite κ>0. Exact rational J_A,J_B,J_C stated in RESULT.md; white-noise variance J/2 has same minimizers.
limitations: Only two distinct leaders, identical finite positive κ, unit-weight windmill edges, equal independent white-noise intensities. No κ=0, unequal gain, weighted graph or other cardinalities.
